pages.c23-p02: Describe superposition and measurement using probabilities
pages.c23-p03: Describe entanglement and interference using simple models
pages.c23-p04: Describe how quantum computers are built and why errors and decoherence are major challenges

q.q: What values can a classical bit hold?
What is a qubit?
Which model is used to explain a qubit in superposition?
q.why: A spinning coin isn't heads or tails yet.

q.q: Which model fits a classical bit?
o: A light switch, on or off

q.q: What kind of physics do quantum computers use?
o: Quantum physics, the physics of very small things
q.why: Quantum rules govern atoms and light.

q.q: Which everyday invention relied on understanding quantum physics?
q.why: Lasers, LEDs and transistors use quantum physics.

q.q: Which statement is TRUE?
o: Quantum computers are faster at everything
Quantum computers help with special problems, not everyday tasks

q.q: What is a classical computer?
o: An ordinary computer that uses bits
An old computer from the past

q.q: Why won't you play games on a quantum computer?
o: They're not suited to everyday tasks and need extreme conditions

q.q: What is superposition?
o: A qubit being in a combination of 0 and 1

q.q: What happens when a qubit is measured?
o: It gives 0 or 1 and loses its superposition

q.q: If you measure a qubit twice in a row, the second result...
o: is the same as the first

q.q: A qubit has a 70% chance of 0. Measured 100 times, about how many 0s?
How many states can 3 qubits represent in superposition?
How many states can 5 qubits represent?
How many states can 10 qubits represent?
What happens to the number of states each time you add a qubit?
Why are quantum programs run many times?
o: Each run gives one random result; the pattern shows the answer

q.q: Can you "peek" at qubits halfway through a calculation without affecting them?
Which is a misunderstanding about quantum computers?
o: They give one result per measurement
They try every answer and show you all of them

q.q: What is entanglement?
o: A link between qubits so their results are connected

q.q: Who called entanglement "spooky action at a distance"?
Two entangled qubits are measured far apart. In a common setup...
o: their results are always opposite and random

q.q: Does entanglement let you send messages faster than light?
o: No: each result on its own is random

q.q: What is interference?
o: Waves adding up or cancelling out

q.q: What happens when a crest meets a trough of equal size?
What happens when two crests meet?
o: They add up into a bigger crest

q.q: Which everyday product uses destructive interference?
How do quantum algorithms find the right answer?
o: Interference makes wrong answers cancel and right answers add up

q.q: What is a quantum algorithm?
o: A sequence of operations on qubits to solve a problem

q.q: The 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for experiments on...
Which company uses superconducting qubits?
q.why: Google and IBM use superconducting circuits.

q.q: What are trapped ions?
o: Charged atoms held by electric fields and controlled by lasers

q.q: Which particles of light can be used as qubits?
What is absolute zero?
Why are superconducting quantum computers kept near absolute zero?
Are superconducting quantum chips colder than outer space?
o: About the same as a freezer

q.q: What is the "chandelier" in a quantum computer?
o: The dilution refrigerator that cools the qubits

q.q: What is decoherence?
o: Qubits losing their quantum state when disturbed

q.q: Which can cause decoherence?
What does quantum error correction do?
o: Combines many physical qubits into one more reliable logical qubit

q.q: What was important about Google's Willow chip (2024)?
o: Errors went down as more qubits were added to error correction

q.q: Is having more qubits automatically better?
o: No: qubit quality (low errors) matters too

q.q: Which is a logical qubit?
o: A reliable qubit built from many physical qubits
q.why: Logical qubits come from error correction.

q.q: Which problem is quantum computing especially suited to?
Who suggested using quantum computers to simulate nature?
How could quantum computers help medicine?
o: By simulating how molecules interact to design new drugs

q.q: How could quantum computers help the environment?
o: Designing better batteries and lower-energy fertiliser production

q.q: What is optimisation?
o: Finding the best option among huge numbers of possibilities
Making a computer faster by deleting files

q.q: Which is an optimisation problem?
o: Finding the best delivery routes for 100 vans
q.why: Choosing the best of many options.

q.q: Which algorithm could break RSA encryption?
Grover's algorithm can...
q.why: It gives a modest speed-up for searching.

q.q: What is quantum advantage?
o: When a quantum computer solves a problem faster than any ordinary computer

q.q: Has quantum advantage been shown for most useful real-world tasks yet?
o: No, mostly for specially chosen test problems

q.q: Which claim is hype?
o: Quantum computers will make every website load instantly

q.q: "Quantum healing bracelets" are best described as...
Why are governments switching to post-quantum cryptography?
o: Future quantum computers could break today's public-key encryption

q.q: What is a quantum sensor?
o: A device using quantum effects to measure tiny changes

q.q: How could quantum navigation help?
Why is navigation without GPS useful?
o: GPS signals can be jammed or blocked

q.q: What is quantum key distribution?
o: Sending encryption keys with particles of light so eavesdropping is detected

q.q: What is the UK National Quantum Strategy?
o: A 10-year plan to make the UK a leading quantum economy

q.q: Where is the UK's National Quantum Computing Centre?
Which programming language is commonly used to program quantum computers?
q.why: Qiskit and Cirq are Python libraries.

q.q: Which subjects are most useful for a quantum career?
Which job might involve designing quantum algorithms?
Which non-science roles are needed in quantum technology?
Which is a possible risk of quantum technology?
o: Breaking current encryption before systems are updated

q.q: Which is a possible benefit of quantum technology?
o: New medicines designed by simulating molecules

q.q: Have quantum navigation systems been tested in the UK?
What is a simulation?
o: Using a computer to model how something behaves

q.q: Which is a sensible question when you read a quantum headline?
o: What problem, compared with what, and has it been checked?

q.q: 2 qubits can represent how many states?
Which is NOT a way to make qubits?
What does "physical qubit" mean?
o: An actual qubit in the hardware
q.why: Many physical qubits make one logical qubit.

q.q: The temperature of outer space is about...
q.why: Space is about 2.7 degrees above absolute zero.

q.q: Measuring a qubit in an equal superposition 1,000 times gives roughly...
Which is a correct statement about entangled qubits?
o: Measuring one tells you about the other
They are always in the same box

q.q: Which helps reduce decoherence?
Which is the most accurate description of today's quantum computers?
o: Promising but small and error-prone research machines
Faster than all supercomputers at everything

q.q: Which describes the "harvest now, decrypt later" threat?
o: Storing encrypted data now to break with future quantum computers

q.q: Which describes quantum clocks?
o: Extremely accurate timekeepers using quantum effects
Clocks with qubits on the face

q.q: Which university in Northern Ireland has quantum research?
Which statement about quantum and AI is fair?
o: Quantum computers might help some kinds of machine learning in future
Quantum computers already run all AI
AI is impossible on classical computers
Quantum computers are a type of chatbot

q.q: The number of states 300 qubits can represent is...
o: more than the atoms in the observable universe

q.q: What does a transistor in an ordinary chip do?
o: Acts as a tiny switch that stores or changes a bit
q.why: Transistors switch bits on and off.

q.q: In the coin model, a coin lying heads-up represents...
o: a classical bit with a definite value

q.q: Roughly how many bits does a modern phone processor flip each second?
A qubit is set so 0 and 1 are equally likely. What's the chance of measuring 1?
Which describes a weighted superposition?
o: 0 and 1 have different probabilities, such as 80:20

q.q: What is a "shot" in quantum computing?
o: One run of a quantum program, ending in a measurement

q.q: Adding a wave +3, -3, +3 to a wave +3, -3, +3 gives...
Adding +1, -1 to -1, +1 gives...
Which three ideas do quantum algorithms combine?
q.why: These are the key quantum ingredients.

q.q: Why can cosmic rays be a problem for quantum computers?
o: They can disturb qubits and cause errors

q.q: Which is a challenge for trapped-ion quantum computers?
o: Scaling up to very large numbers of qubits

q.q: What do quantum computers need to be useful for big problems like medicine design?
Which job could a quantum computer help a car company with?
Which everyday task would NOT get faster on a quantum computer?
Which is a reason the UK invests in quantum technology?
o: To create new industries, jobs and security
q.why: It's an economic and security priority.
